---
title: "Issue label check"
description: "Removes the approval label if the wrong person set it or the issue changed afterwards."
---

`issue-label-check.yml` guards the label that approves an issue for a bot.
An approval only counts if the right person gave it, for the text as it
stands. No Claude is involved, and the calling repository is not checked
out.

- **Label set:** if the person who set it is not in `allowed-logins`, the
  label is removed, with one short comment saying why. Only the exact login
  counts, not the person's access level: a maintainer who isn't listed is
  treated like anyone else, and so is a bot.
- **Issue edited:** if the issue carries the label, it is removed, with a
  comment that the issue needs approving again. This applies to everyone,
  listed people included, because a changed title or body is no longer
  what was approved.

Anything else does nothing, including the removal itself, so the check
can't set itself off.

## Example

{{< example issue-label-check.yml >}}

`issues` events only start workflows from the default branch, so the
caller has to be there. Create the label in the repository first.

## Limits

The check runs after the fact, usually within seconds, so it is not the
gate itself. Whatever acts on the label has to verify the approval again
when it starts. In particular:

- For a few seconds, a label set by the wrong person stands on the issue.
- Renaming another label to the approval label puts it on issues without
  a `labeled` event, so this check doesn't see it.
- Logins are compared exactly, including case. A login spelled
  differently from the GitHub account means that person's own approvals
  are removed.

Approving within seconds of your own edit can be undone by the check for
that edit; set the label again.
